title: Assessing the Profitability of Timely Opening Range Breakout on Index Futures Markets
one_line: A 'timely' opening range breakout — range from the start of the stock market's active hours to a probe time, trade the first break, exit at the end of active hours — earned > 8%/yr after 0.01% costs on E-mini DJIA, S&P 500, Nasdaq-100, HSI and TAIEX (2001-2013); best probe times were 1 minute for ES and NQ, 4 for YM.

findings.statement: All five index futures: annual returns > 8%, one-tailed p < 3%, after 0.01% per-trade costs.
Best probe times: S&P 500 1 min, Nasdaq 1 min, DJIA 4 min, HSI 151 min, TAIEX 37 min; Nasdaq best ≈ 17.5%/yr.
findings.evidence: Probe time picked on the full sample (in-sample selection).

findings.statement: Classic Brock et al. trading-range breakouts (10-day holds) were not significant on most markets.
On TAIEX, the breakout direction lines up with institutional (especially foreign) net buying.

why.pattern: Execution mechanics / informed institutional order flow concentrated at the open.

reported_results.headline: A 'timely' opening range breakout — range from the start of the stock market's active hours to a probe time, trade the first break, exit at the end of active hours — earned > 8%/yr after 0.01% costs on E-mini DJIA, S&P 500, Nasdaq-100, HSI and TAIEX (2001-2013); best probe times were 1 minute for ES and NQ, 4 for YM.

tradable_edge: Covered by T5 (opening range breakout) in VOLATILITY_BREAKOUT_RESEARCH_TESTS.md; adds a 1-minute opening-range variant for ES/NQ. Note the 0.01% cost assumption (~1 ES point at 6,000+) and in-sample probe selection; the 2026 MNQ falsification study found ORB not significant after costs.

decay_risk.reason: Ends 2013; recent MNQ study found ORB long not significant (t = 0.88).

data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
